## Quick “Road‑Map” – A Mental‑Health Journal App | Phase | What to Do | Key Deliverables | Suggested Tech | |-------|------------|------------------|----------------| | 🎯 **Goal & Personas** | Define *why* the app exists (e.g., self‑reflection, therapy prep, tracking mood). Identify target users (students, workers, therapy clients). | User‑journey map, user‑story charts | - | | 🖥️ **Design** | Wireframe core screens: On‑board, Daily Entry, Calendar, Stats, Settings. Draft UI/UX with color psychology (soft blues/pinks). | Figma/Sketch prototypes, style guide | Figma / Adobe XD | | ⚙️ **Tech Stack** | Choose mobile framework + backend. | MVP tech‑spec document | React‑Native or Flutter; Firebase / Supabase; Realm / SQLite for local storage | | 🛠️ **Core Features** | • Daily text entry
• Mood tags & sliders
• Image/video attachment
• Submission confirmation (thoughtful prompt)
• Calendar view & trend charts
• Search & filter by keyword / tag
• Optional sharing / therapist sync | Feature backlog | - | | 🔐 **Security / Privacy** | Local encryption, no PII storage, local backups, secure cloud sync (end‑to‑end). | Security architecture diagram | Firebase Auth + Firestore; AES-GCM local encryption | | 🚀 **Prototype & MVP** | Build a minimal viable product with 1–2 core screens. | Working swipeable form, save to local DB | TDD harness (Jest / Flutter Test) | | 📈 **Testing & Feedback** | Recruit 5–10 beta users, collect NPS, mental‑health metrics (e.g., PHQ‑9) pre/post. | User‑feedback report | Qualtrics / Typeform | | 🎨 **Polish & Launch** | Final UI tweaks, push notifications (soft mood check‑ins), analytics. | Play/ App Store listing, marketing copy | Firebase Crashlytics, Amplitude | | 🙋 **Maintenance & Growth** | Iterate strategy, add AI insights, therapist workflow, integration with wearables. | Road‑map update | - | --- ## 1. Start With a User‑Focused Narrative > **“Jordan** is 28, works in tech, and struggles with stress. Each night before bed, she opens a simple app, writes a 200‑word note, tags her mood “anxious”, and maybe attaches a photo of her sunset view. A week later, she looks back at a calendar that shows a *blue‑bar trend* of high anxiety. The app nudges her to share the entry or copy it to her therapist. That’s the core journey.** ### Interview Questions for Target Users - What triggers you to journal (time of day, event, mood)? - Which prompts help you express yourself? - Do you want to share with a therapist or keep it private? - How important is visual mood tracking? - Are you concerned about privacy or data security? --- ## 2. Wireframes (Low‑Fi) Below are skeleton screens you can export to Figma or Sketch: 1. **Splash / On‑board** - Splash screen → 3 swipe‑through panels explaining: *Write, Track, Reflect* - CTA: **“Start Writing”** 2. **Daily Entry** - Canvas: Date at top, Tag selector (emoji/mood slider) - Text editor: 200‑word limit, preview icon - Attach: 📷📹 button - Optional Prompt: *“How did you cope today?”* - **Save** button (top‑right) 3. **Calendar View** - Month grid, each day cell colored by average mood - Tap → Day view (entries list) 4. **Day View** - List of entries for that day. - Each entry shows: mood tag, snippet, attachment thumbnail. - Swipe left → *Delete* / *Share*. 5. **Stats & Trends** - Line chart: Mood over days/weeks. - Bar chart: Frequency of moods. - 7‑day average panel, “Biggest Improvement” snippet. 6. **Settings** - Profile (name, email ) - Privacy: Locally encrypted / Cloud sync toggle - Reminders: Daily push, at chosen time - Export: PDF, CSV --- ## 3. Technology Choices | Need | Option | Why | |------|--------|-----| | **Cross‑platform** | **Flutter** or **React‑Native** | One codebase, good community | | **Local persistence** | **Hive** (Flutter) or **SQLite** | Lightweight, fast | | **Encryption** | **flutter_sodium** / **crypto** package | End‑to‑end local encryption | | **Cloud sync (optional)** | **Firebase Firestore** + **Auth** | Zero‑code backend, auto‑sync | | **Charts** | **charts_flutter** / **fl_chart** | Simple line/bar charts | | **Testing** | **Flutter Test** / **Jest** + **Detox** | BDD and UI test automation | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions | Build, lint, test on push | > **Pro tip** – For early beta, start with only local storage. Cold‑backup to user‑owned cloud (e.g., iCloud Drive, Google Drive export) once you validate the privacy claim. --- ## 4. Data Model (Simplified) ``` Entry { id: String // UUID date: DateTime // Date text: String // Note mood: String // Enum: happy, anxious, sad, etc. moodScore: Int // 0–10 slider attachments: [URL] // optional created: DateTime updated: DateTime } ``` All entries are stored encrypted locally. If sync enabled, they are also sent to Firestore with a timestamp. --- ## 5. UI/UX Tips - **Color psychology**: use soft pastels for UI; mood colors (blue for calm, red for upset). - **Emotion emojis**: quick taps for mood tags. - **Progressive disclosure**: simple “Today” entry first; deeper stats appear after 3 days. - **Micro‑animations**: a soft “tick” tick when entry saved; a gentle particle when a new insight is generated. - **Dark mode**: essential for nighttime use. --- ## 6. Security & Privacy | Concern | Implementation | |---------|----------------| | **Data at rest** | AES‑256 GCM on local DB (key derived from user‑password or device biometrics). | | **Data in transit** | HTTPS + OAuth (Firestore). | |
